purpose: How a gold-plating bench turns scattered one-off jobs into a durable trade book: qualifying and refusing jeweller, repair-counter, restorer and brand accounts, writing the account terms that fix price basis, turnaround class, liability ceiling and the plated-finish disclosure the account must carry to its own customer, moving and holding other people's goods under a custody and carrier-class discipline, keeping promises the bench queue can actually support and saying so early when it cannot, adjudicating returned work by cause against the record, and reading the replate cycle, job history, ledger and concentration signals that decide which accounts to grow, wean or end.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the shop is a small commercial gold-plating bench that plates goods it does not own, sent by other businesses, and returns them

commercial plating chemistry is purchased and run per its technical data sheet; every bath setpoint, cycle time and thickness capability referenced here is consumed from the bench specialists, never re-derived commercially

prices, discounts, turnaround windows, credit limits and insured values are mechanisms and classes in this KB; the shop's own reconciled costs, its policy documents and its carrier's terms supply the actual figures

insurance cover, credit terms and contract wording are commercial arrangements whose specifics come from the shop's own broker, accountant and jurisdiction; this KB describes the classes and the decisions, not the products
an account is a business that resells or returns the plated piece to a consumer, so the shop's disclosure duty does not end at the account's counter
the book is written down: accounts, terms, job history and ledger live in records that survive the owner's memory and a busy week
exclusions: constructing the price of a job — the cost mechanism of labour time, gold consumed from area times thickness times karat, consumables, risk premium and finishing, the service-menu classes themselves, minimum charges, batching economics, quote-validity windows against metal-price movement and the decline-unprofitable-work verdict — the sibling Service Design & Job Pricing KB owns those; this KB consumes the mechanism and owns only the account-level structure wrapped around it

documenting a customer's individual piece at intake — condition photographs, stone and solder-joint notes, the heirloom and irreplaceable-item risk acknowledgment and its signature, the wording of a refusal to a piece owner, approval gates for irreversible steps and the dispute-avoiding handover record — the sibling Client Intake & Expectation Management KB owns those artifacts, together with the tagging and the turnaround promise given directly to a piece owner at the counter; this KB invokes them per piece inside a trade parcel and owns only the parcel-and-lot level custody, count and identity of a trade consignment and the account-level turnaround classes

how the plating is performed — surface preparation, bath make-up and analysis, rack and current distribution, strike and deposit parameters, colour control, thickness and adhesion verification, defect diagnosis and rework procedure — the bench specialists own those; here a defect is a cause routed back to them and a class is an elapsed time in the queue

approving a regulated marking or label claim for a finished piece — plated, heavy plate, vermeil over sterling, gold filled and rolled gold are threshold-bound classes in the selling jurisdiction, and nickel-release limits, waste and discharge duties are obligation classes; this KB records what was deposited on what and tells the account to verify current rules in its own market, and never blesses the claim

wear-life, durability or permanent-finish guarantees of any length to an account or its customer; the replate interval is described as a mechanism plus the intervals the shop has actually observed, offered as an expectation and never as a promise

personalised legal, tax, insurance-product, credit or debt-recovery advice, and metal hedging or forward buying as investment activity; the shop's accountant, broker and legal adviser own those decisions
recruiting, employment terms and workshop layout or equipment purchasing decisions, which sit with the shop-operations side rather than with the account book

glossary.definition: A standing relationship with a business — jeweller, repair counter, restorer, watchmaker, brand — that sends the bench goods it does not own, on written terms, expecting a repeatable price basis, turnaround class and liability position rather than a fresh negotiation per job.

The unit trade work arrives and leaves in: many pieces from one account moving together under one manifest, one declared value and one carrier class, which is why custody, insurance and reconciliation are parcel-level disciplines while condition documentation stays per piece.

Counting and identifying every piece received against the sender's list at the moment of opening, and reporting any short, extra, misdescribed or wrong item to the account inside the window the terms name — before any piece enters a batch and before ownership of the discrepancy becomes arguable.

The identifier that binds a parcel's pieces to their account through every bench stage, carried as a physical tag, a tagged compartment or a bagged sub-lot, so no piece is ever an anonymous item of gold-coloured jewellery on a tray.

The written limit on how much of an account's property the shop will accept in one parcel, and separately on the aggregate value of all accounts' goods on the premises at once; the instrument that converts a cover arrangement into an operational refusal or a split shipment.

The movement option chosen for a parcel — specialist valuables carrier, general courier, insured postal class, account hand-carry, shop collection — each with its own answer to whether jewellery is covered at all, at what declared-value cap, and under which packaging, tracking and reporting conditions.

A named delivery promise (scheduled batch day, standard window, expedited, by-arrangement after inspection) derived from queue arithmetic rather than invented per call, each stating what starts the clock, what pauses it and what it excludes, so realised performance can be audited by class.

The defined moment a turnaround class begins to run — goods received and reconciled on the bench, not goods posted or promised — together with the pause conditions (an unanswered approval, a piece found unfit for the requested class) that stop it honestly.

The natural return of a plated piece for renewal because a plated surface wears; its interval is moved by deposit class and thickness, the underplate beneath it, the use class of the piece and the wearer's own chemistry and habits, and is estimated from observed returns rather than promised.

The share of the book's revenue and of committed bench hours held by one account or one class of account, read together with what would happen to the week if it stopped — a decision to be taken deliberately with a stated tolerance, not a fact discovered after the account leaves.

nodes.definition: State plainly what the trade book is before a single account is opened: the set of standing relationships with businesses that send this bench other people's gold to plate, whose value is the predictability of the flow rather than the size of any one invoice. The charter fixes four premises the rest of the subdomain rests on. First, the shop takes custody of goods it does not own, so its exposure on a parcel is the value of the goods and not the value of the job — a tray of a jeweller's customer rings is worth many times the plating on them. Second, every promise made to an account — turnaround class, thickness class, liability position — must be derivable from what the bench can actually do, because a trade partner buys repeatability and will forgive a slower honest class far longer than a fast broken one. Third, the plated character of the work travels with the goods in writing, because the account resells to a consumer who must never be told the surface is solid gold. Fourth, the book only counts as an asset if it is written down: accounts held in the owner's head cannot be reviewed, re-priced, covered during illness, staffed or handed on.

included: what an account and a book are
the custodial-exposure premise
promises derived from bench capability
the disclosure-travels-with-the-goods premise
the write-it-down rule
excluded: per-job price construction
per-piece condition documentation for a piece owner
bath setpoints and bench procedure

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the first full year of accounts shows a premise that was never actually followed or never actually needed

pros.claim: Premises written before the first account stop every later term being invented under pressure at the counter
pros.example: a repair-counter chain asking for same-week turnaround on its first parcel meets an already-written commitment class instead of an improvised yes that breaks the following month

pros.claim: Naming custodial exposure as separate from job value sizes the liability conversation correctly from day one
pros.example: a two-figure flash refresh on a parcel of forty customer rings is treated as a high-value custody event, not a small job

cons.claim: A charter written from an empty book encodes guesses that the first real accounts will contradict
cons.example: assuming trade parcels arrive by insured carrier when the local jewellers actually hand-carry on their Thursday delivery round

cons.claim: Written premises can harden into bureaucracy that a two-person bench resents and quietly stops following
cons.example: a charter demanding a signed acknowledgment for a five-piece parcel from a jeweller two doors away

failure_modes: treating the book as a list of friendly names rather than a set of written terms and job histories
promising from ambition rather than capability, so one busy month breaks three accounts at once
letting the disclosure premise stop at the account's counter because the account is a professional
acceptance_tests: the charter states the custodial-exposure premise, the capability-derived-promise rule, the disclosure-passthrough premise and the write-it-down rule in terms a new bench hand can apply without asking the owner
revisit_triggers: the shop adds a service class or a substrate it could not previously handle
an account type arrives that none of the premises anticipated, such as a brand sending unworn production runs

nodes.definition: Separate the two channels the bench serves, because nearly every operating rule differs between them and mixing them is how a shop quietly loses money and gets into disclosure trouble. In retail the piece belongs to the person at the counter, the shop owns the disclosure conversation and the expectation setting, intake is per piece with photographs and a signature, the decision-maker has no idea what a strike or an underplate is, and the price must carry the full cost of that conversation. In trade the piece belongs to the account's client, the account owns the end-consumer relationship and therefore carries the disclosure onward, work arrives in parcels with a manifest, the decision-maker is a professional who can specify a class in three words, approvals come back by message rather than by appointment, and the per-piece overhead of explaining, photographing and quoting collapses — which is the only honest reason a trade rate can sit below a walk-in rate. Naming the channel on every job ticket keeps the two from contaminating each other: trade rates must not leak to walk-ins who are buying the conversation as well as the gold, and retail intake ceremony must not be skipped for a piece merely because it arrived inside a jeweller's parcel.

included: who owns the piece and the end-consumer relationship in each channel
intake unit and approval mechanics per channel
the identified overhead saving that funds a trade level
channel labelling on the job ticket
excluded: the price mechanism itself
the wording of a consumer-facing disclosure at a retail counter
the account's own retail pricing

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: reconciliation shows trade jobs consuming retail-level conversation time on a class of accounts

pros.claim: An explicit channel label stops a trade rate leaking to a walk-in job that carries far more unpriced conversation
pros.example: a jeweller's brother-in-law arriving with one ring and asking for the trade price on work that needs a full intake and a wear-expectation talk

pros.claim: Knowing the account carries the downstream disclosure defines exactly what documentation must leave with the parcel
pros.example: the returned job ticket naming the deposit class in plain words so the jeweller can repeat it to the ring's owner

cons.claim: The separation blurs for hybrid partners who are sometimes a reseller and sometimes the piece owner
cons.example: an antique dealer sending both shop stock they own and customer commissions they merely hold

cons.claim: A trade discount justified by collapsed overhead invites the assumption that every account deserves one
cons.example: a low-volume account sending two mixed pieces a quarter, each needing as much conversation as a walk-in

failure_modes: skipping per-piece documentation because the sender is a professional, then having no record when a stone is disputed
granting a trade level to an account whose behaviour generates full retail overhead
assuming the account passed the wear expectation to its customer without any written trace that it could
acceptance_tests: every job ticket carries a channel label, and for each channel the record states who owns the piece, who owns the disclosure conversation and which intake path was used
revisit_triggers: an account starts sending its own customers to the bench directly
hybrid parcels mixing account-owned stock and customer property become common

nodes.definition: Sort the possible trade partners into classes, because what each sends, how often, and what it demands differ enough to decide whether the account is worth having at all. Independent jewellers send worn customer rings, chains and lockets for refresh in small mixed parcels, at irregular cadence, with heirloom content and a real need for refusal judgement. Repair-counter and multi-branch chains send high-volume, low-value refresh work on a predictable schedule and buy almost purely on turnaround reliability. Antique and estate dealers send fragile, mixed-metal, sometimes irreplaceable stock where the right answer is often no, and where a wrong yes cannot be undone. Watchmakers send cases, bezels and bracelets where masking, fit tolerance and not touching a movement dominate every other consideration. Silversmiths and restorers send large-area hollowware whose feasibility is decided by rack design and tank capacity long before price. Costume and fashion brands send unworn production runs where batch consistency, substrate declaration and the marking-class question matter most. Trophy, engraving and giftware shops send flat, easily racked, price-driven work that batches beautifully and pays the overhead on quiet weeks. Each class gets a written note on typical parcel value, cadence, dominant demand — price, speed or judgement — and the refusal pressure it will apply.

included: the partner classes and their work mix
cadence and typical parcel value per class
dominant demand and refusal pressure per class
which classes suit this bench's capability
excluded: vetting a specific named prospect
the price schedule offered to a class
how to find prospects through referral

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the book's own results show a class behaving differently from its written note on cadence, value or demand

pros.claim: Classing prospects tells the shop in advance which demand it is being asked to satisfy, so the sales conversation is about the right thing
pros.example: meeting a repair chain with realised on-time performance by class instead of a price list they were never going to read

pros.claim: A class note makes the bad fits visible before they become accounts
pros.example: recognising that hollowware restorers will ask for tank capacity this bench does not have, before a first parcel of trays arrives

cons.claim: Classes flatten real businesses and can prejudge a prospect that does not behave like its class
cons.example: an antique dealer with immaculate manifests and modest, well-chosen work being treated as high-refusal-pressure by default

cons.claim: Chasing the highest-cadence class can crowd out the judgement-heavy accounts that carry the better margin
cons.example: a bench filled with trophy work while jewellers who send heavy replates wait behind it

failure_modes: courting every class at once and building a book with no coherent capacity plan
mistaking a class's volume for its profitability without reconciling the work back to cost
ignoring that one class arrives with irreplaceable items and needs refusal criteria before it needs a price
acceptance_tests: each named partner class carries its work mix, its cadence, its dominant demand and the specific bench capability or refusal criterion it will test
revisit_triggers: the shop gains or loses a capability that changes which classes it can serve, such as a larger tank or a barrel line
a class the book relied on changes its buying behaviour across several accounts at once

nodes.definition: Make the plated character of the work travel with the goods, in writing, into the account's own paperwork. The shop's honesty duty does not end because the customer is a business: the account will resell or hand the piece back to a consumer, so every job ticket, invoice and returned parcel states the service class performed, the deposit in plain words — a thin decorative refresh over existing plate, or a rebuilt underplate carrying a wear-duty gold layer — and the plain fact that this is a plated surface that wears, not solid gold through. Marking and label terms are a separate, regulated matter: plated, heavy plate, vermeil over sterling, gold filled and rolled gold are classes bound to thickness and substrate thresholds in the selling jurisdiction, so the shop records what it deposited and on what substrate, names the class question, and tells the account to verify the current rules in its own market rather than blessing the claim. Skin-contact and nickel-release duties are handled the same way, as obligation classes routed to the compliance side and to the account's own responsibility. An account that asks for documentation implying solid gold, that wants the word vermeil on a base-metal piece, or that resists any wear language reaching its customer, is a refusal — not a negotiation, not a discount, and not a problem to be solved with careful phrasing.

included: what documentation leaves with a trade parcel
plain-words statement of deposit class and plated character
marking terms named as jurisdiction-bound classes to verify
refusal of accounts that will misrepresent
excluded: deciding the numeric threshold for a marking term in any jurisdiction
the account's own consumer-facing sales copy
the wording used with a walk-in piece owner

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a regulator, a trade body or an account's own market changes what must be disclosed or how a class may be named

pros.claim: Written class language on the returned ticket gives the account the words to repeat, so the disclosure survives the handover
pros.example: a returned parcel whose ticket reads that a thin decorative refresh was applied over the existing plate on a base-metal shank, which the jeweller reads straight to the customer

pros.claim: Refusing the misrepresentation request early costs one account and protects every other one
pros.example: declining a reseller who wanted invoices omitting the word plated so its listings could imply solid gold

cons.claim: Insisting on wear and class language can lose accounts to a competitor who will write whatever is asked
cons.example: a volume reseller moving its work to a bench that issues bare invoices with no deposit description

cons.claim: Naming marking terms as jurisdiction-bound classes frustrates an account that wants a yes or no about the word vermeil
cons.example: a brand pushing for confirmation that its sterling line may be marked, which only its own market's current rules can answer

failure_modes: issuing a bare invoice with no deposit description, leaving the account free to imply anything downstream
blessing a marking or fineness claim the shop has no standing to approve
treating a request to omit the word plated as a paperwork preference rather than a refusal trigger
acceptance_tests: every returned parcel carries documentation naming the service class, the deposit in plain words, the substrate and the plated-surface statement, with no marking claim asserted by the shop
the account file records that the disclosure clause was accepted, and any request to soften or omit it is logged with the decision taken
revisit_triggers: an account's own listings or window cards are seen describing the shop's work as solid gold
marking, fineness or nickel-release rules change in a market the book serves

nodes.definition: Decide whether to open an account before quoting one, using a short repeatable check rather than gratitude for the enquiry. Confirm the business is what it says it is — trading identity, a real premises, how long it has been buying plating and from whom, and a trade reference from a peer who has been paid by it. Then ask the three bench questions about the work mix it intends to send: can this shop physically do it, given substrate, size, rack, masking and tank capacity; is what the account expects achievable at the class it wants to pay for; and does the mix carry item types this shop refuses, such as irreplaceable pieces whose loss no price could answer. Add the two commercial checks — will they work on written terms at all, and what does their payment behaviour look like — and reach one of three verdicts: open, open on restricted terms (prepay or on account with a capped parcel value, a sample batch first, no standing schedule until reconciliation), or decline with a plain reason. A sample first parcel is the cheapest qualification instrument that exists: one small batch exposes their expectations, their packing habits, their manifest discipline, their approval responsiveness and their payment behaviour inside a single cycle, before any standing commitment is made.

included: identity and trade-reference checks
capability and expectation feasibility against the intended mix
the willingness-to-accept-terms and payment-behaviour checks
open / restricted / decline verdict and the sample-parcel instrument
excluded: the price schedule itself
credit scoring or personal financial assessment of the account's principals
per-piece refusal of an individual item once an account exists

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an account that passed qualification fails on a dimension the check does not currently look at

pros.claim: A sample parcel buys more information about an account than any amount of discussion
pros.example: a first ten-piece batch revealing that the sender expects stripping and stone-tightening included in a refresh price

pros.claim: A written verdict with a reason makes a later decline defensible and repeatable rather than personal
pros.example: declining a dealer whose parcels would routinely exceed the shop's per-parcel ceiling, with the ceiling cited

cons.claim: Qualification friction can lose a good account to a bench that simply says yes
cons.example: a busy repair chain moving on while waiting for a trade reference to answer

cons.claim: A first sample parcel is a small and possibly unrepresentative sample of the account's real behaviour
cons.example: an account sending its cleanest, simplest work first and its problem pieces once terms are granted

failure_modes: opening an account on enthusiasm and discovering the mix is outside the bench's capability after the second parcel
skipping the payment-behaviour check on an account that arrives with impressive volume
accepting an account whose expectations can only be met by overstating what the deposit is
acceptance_tests: each opened account file contains the identity check, the capability and expectation assessment against the intended mix, the payment-behaviour note and a dated open / restricted / decline verdict with its reason
no account reaches a standing schedule before at least one reconciled parcel has been completed and costed
revisit_triggers: an account's actual work mix diverges from what qualification assumed
a qualification check that has never once changed a verdict, or one that keeps missing a failure the book later pays for

nodes.definition: Set the account-level price basis: which standing schedule this account works from, and which identified cost differences fund the gap between it and a walk-in price. The cost mechanism itself is not re-derived here — labour time, gold consumed from area times thickness times karat, consumables, risk premium and finishing come from the pricing subdomain — what belongs to the account is the structure wrapped around that mechanism. That structure names the piece classes this account actually sends and the standing figure or formula for each, states whether the schedule is metal-inclusive or adjusted against a stated metal basis and how movement in that basis is passed through, records the volume or cadence expectation the level assumes, and fixes the review point at which the schedule is re-derived from reconciled jobs rather than renewed by habit. The discipline is simple and unpopular: a trade level must be funded by a saving the shop can name — parcels instead of counter conversations, batched racks instead of single-piece runs, standing specifications instead of per-job quoting, predictable scheduling instead of interruption — and never by hoping that volume will eventually repair a rate that was below cost on the day it was agreed.

included: which standing schedule applies to this account
the named savings that fund a trade level
metal-basis pass-through and the schedule review point
cadence or volume expectation attached to the level
excluded: deriving the underlying job cost
the service-menu class definitions themselves
quote-validity mechanics for one-off walk-in quotes
competitor price matching

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: reconciled job costing shows an account's standing schedule sitting below cost on a class it sends often

pros.claim: Tying every trade level to a named saving keeps discounting honest and reversible
pros.example: a batched-flat-goods level justified by full racks and one setup, withdrawn when the account starts sending five-piece mixed parcels

pros.claim: A standing schedule removes per-job quoting friction, which is itself one of the savings the level rests on
pros.example: an account sending a weekly parcel of known classes that needs no quote round-trip at all

cons.claim: Standing schedules go stale against metal movement and against the bench's own changing costs
cons.example: a schedule agreed at one metal basis still being honoured after a sustained move, quietly eating the margin on every heavy class

cons.claim: Naming the saving invites the account to argue about whether the saving is real
cons.example: an account insisting its parcels batch perfectly while the bench log shows part-filled racks

failure_modes: granting a level on promised volume that never arrives and never withdrawing it
leaving the metal-basis treatment unstated so every metal move becomes an argument
reviewing schedules only when an account complains, which selects for exactly the wrong direction of change
acceptance_tests: each account's schedule names the piece classes it covers, the savings that fund the level, the metal-basis treatment and a dated review point
at review, the schedule is compared against reconciled job costs for that account rather than against last year's schedule
revisit_triggers: the metal basis moves beyond the band the schedule assumed
the account's parcel size, mix or cadence changes so the named saving no longer occurs

nodes.definition: Fix in advance, and in writing, how much of other people's property this shop is willing to hold and to move at one time. Two ceilings matter and they are not the same. The per-parcel declared value governs how a consignment may be shipped and what a carrier class or cover arrangement will actually answer for; the on-premises aggregate is the total declared value of all accounts' goods inside the shop at once, bounded by the shop's security arrangements and its own cover conditions. The ceiling is what turns the sentence we are insured into an operational rule: a parcel above the per-parcel figure is split across shipments or moved by a different class before it is sent, an account's standing instruction to consolidate a quarter's work into one big consignment is refused rather than accommodated, and the week is planned so the aggregate does not silently climb past its limit while several accounts' parcels sit waiting for a batch day. The actual limits, exclusions, security conditions and reporting duties come from the shop's own policy documents and the carrier's terms — read them, confirm what must hold for cover to survive, verify the requirements applicable in your jurisdiction, and treat any figure not written in those documents as unknown rather than assumed.

included: per-parcel declared value ceiling
on-premises aggregate ceiling
split, refuse or reclass decisions when a ceiling is exceeded
planning the bench week against the aggregate
excluded: choosing or advising on an insurance product
the wording and exclusions of any specific policy
valuation of an individual heirloom piece

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the shop's cover conditions, security arrangements or a carrier's declared-value cap change

pros.claim: A written ceiling converts an abstract cover arrangement into a decision the bench can make without the owner present
pros.example: a Saturday parcel arriving above the ceiling being held sealed and unopened until the owner authorises the split

pros.claim: The aggregate ceiling catches the risk nobody watches, which builds up quietly across accounts rather than in one parcel
pros.example: four accounts' parcels waiting together for the same batch day while each alone was comfortably inside the limit

cons.claim: Ceilings cost convenience and can annoy the accounts the shop most wants
cons.example: a chain's quarterly consolidation being refused and split into three shipments it has to book separately

cons.claim: A declared value is only as good as the valuation behind it, and trade goods are often valued casually by the sender
cons.example: a manifest valuing a customer's ring at scrap when its replacement to the customer is a jeweller's retail cost

failure_modes: letting a busy week push the on-premises aggregate past the limit without anyone noticing
accepting a sender's declared value without asking what basis it was valued on
treating the ceiling as advisory when the account is important
acceptance_tests: the per-parcel and on-premises ceilings are written, dated, traceable to the shop's own policy and carrier documents, and known to whoever opens the door
every parcel exceeding the per-parcel ceiling has a recorded split, reclass or refusal decision rather than an exception
revisit_triggers: cover, security arrangements or carrier terms change
the book grows enough that ordinary weeks routinely approach the aggregate ceiling

nodes.definition: Know the movement classes available for trade goods and what each actually answers for, because the difference between a covered loss and an uncovered one is usually decided before the parcel leaves the bench. The practical classes are: specialist jewellery and valuables carriers, whose contracts are written for precious goods and whose conditions are correspondingly specific; general parcel couriers, whose terms very commonly exclude or severely cap jewellery and precious metals whatever value is declared at booking; national postal insured or registered services with their own declared-value caps, packaging rules and proof-of-posting requirements; the account's own hand-carry on a delivery round, which removes the carrier but not the risk and needs a signed handover at both ends; and the shop's own collection run, which moves the exposure onto the shop's vehicle and whatever arrangement covers goods in transit with the owner. Each class is chosen against three questions, in order: is this commodity covered at all, is the declared value inside the class cap, and which packaging, tracking, signature, timing and reporting conditions must hold for cover to survive a claim. Cover for goods in transit and cover for goods on the premises are separate arrangements, and the gap between them — a parcel handed over, a piece left in a van overnight — is where real losses fall. Policies, limits and wordings are commercial documents rather than advice this KB can give: read them, ask the broker, and verify the rules that apply in your jurisdiction.

included: the movement classes and what each covers in principle
the three selection questions per parcel
packaging, tracking and signature conditions as cover-survival requirements
the transit-versus-premises cover boundary
excluded: recommending an insurer, broker or policy
stating any specific limit, premium or exclusion as fact
customs, export and duty handling for cross-border parcels

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a carrier's published terms or the shop's cover conditions change, or a claim reveals a condition that was misread

pros.claim: Choosing the class by the three questions prevents the commonest silent failure, which is a covered-looking parcel on a carrier that excludes jewellery outright
pros.example: a high-value replate parcel moved on a valuables service after the general courier's terms were read and found to exclude the commodity

pros.claim: Writing the packaging and signature conditions into the routine keeps cover alive through the messy moments
pros.example: a driver refusing to wait for a signature being handled by the standing rule that unsigned handover is not permitted

cons.claim: The classes that genuinely cover jewellery cost more and constrain timing, which collides with cheap fast expectations
cons.example: an account used to posting parcels casually resisting the cost and the booking window of a valuables service

cons.claim: Conditions are detailed and change, so a class understood correctly last year can be wrong this year
cons.example: a postal service revising its declared-value cap for insured items after the shop's routine was written around the old one

failure_modes: assuming that declaring a value makes an excluded commodity covered
using an inbound class the account chose without checking that it satisfies the shop's own conditions
leaving the transit-to-premises handover moment undefined so neither arrangement clearly applies
acceptance_tests: each account's terms name the carrier class for inbound and outbound parcels and the conditions the shop must meet for cover to hold
for any parcel sent, the record shows the class used, the declared value, the packaging class and the tracking or signature evidence retained
revisit_triggers: a carrier changes its terms, caps or excluded commodities

nodes.definition: Model what this bench can actually deliver in a week before promising anything to anybody, because a turnaround class is arithmetic rather than enthusiasm. The model counts the constraints that really bind: attended bench hours as opposed to calendar hours; how many racks or barrel loads a bath can take in a session and how many sessions the day allows; the fixed sequence time a job cannot be compressed below, which for plated work means preparation and cleaning, strike, deposit, rinse, dry, any cure or topcoat step, and the inspection that must follow before anything is packed; the batch cadence for classes that only run when a rack is full or a bath has been brought up and checked; the share of capacity already committed to work standing in the queue; and the interruptions that are not optional, such as bath analysis, filtration, maintenance and the shop's own retail counter. What comes out is a queue position and a realistic completion window for a new parcel, plus the honest observation a bench owner learns the hard way — a job's elapsed time is mostly queue, drying and inspection, not plating minutes, so quoting from plating minutes produces promises that break. Bath setpoints, cycle times and process parameters belong to the bench specialists and come from the product's technical data sheet; this unit consumes only the elapsed time a class costs and how many of them fit in a week.

included: attended-hours and session-capacity counting
fixed sequence elapsed time per class
batch cadence and queue commitment
the derived completion window for a new parcel
excluded: bath setpoints, cycle chemistry and process parameters
equipment purchasing decisions
the price of the time consumed

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: logged elapsed times or a change in equipment, staffing or batch cadence moves the weekly throughput

pros.claim: A queue-derived window can be defended and audited, and it improves every time a job's realised elapsed time is logged
pros.example: quoting a parcel from its position behind two committed racks rather than from the two hours the plating itself takes

pros.claim: Counting the non-optional interruptions stops the model from promising a fantasy week
pros.example: reserving the morning that bath analysis and filtration actually consume before any parcel is scheduled into it

cons.claim: The model is only as good as its logged elapsed times, and a young shop has few
cons.example: a first heavy replate on hollowware taking three times the assumed handling because racking had to be invented

cons.claim: Capacity that is modelled honestly is usually smaller than the owner believes, which is unwelcome when a big account is being courted
cons.example: discovering the shop can commit to only one scheduled batch day a week for a chain that wants two

failure_modes: quoting from plating minutes and ignoring queue, drying, cure and inspection
counting calendar hours as bench hours and losing the counter, the phone and the maintenance to optimism
leaving no slack at all, so one bath problem cascades into every promised date that week
acceptance_tests: the model states attended hours, session capacity, fixed sequence time per class and current committed load, and produces a completion window rather than a single date
realised elapsed times are logged per job and fed back into the model's assumptions
revisit_triggers: equipment, staffing or bath configuration changes the session capacity

nodes.definition: Offer turnaround as a small set of named classes rather than a date invented on each phone call. A workable set for a plating bench is a scheduled batch class, where parcels received by a stated cut-off go onto the next batch day; a standard class quoted as a window rather than a date; an expedited class that buys queue priority at a price funded by the disruption it actually causes to other committed work; and a by-arrangement class for anything needing stripping, stone removal, repair referral or a rebuilt underplate, where the honest answer is that the parcel is inspected first and a window is given afterwards. Every class states three things without which it is not a class: what starts the clock — goods received and reconciled on the bench, never goods posted or promised — what pauses it, such as an unanswered approval or a piece found unfit for the class requested, and what it excludes. Named classes make the promise auditable, which is the real point: at review the shop can ask what proportion of each class landed inside its window and act on the answer, a question that is impossible to ask when every job carried a bespoke date agreed in a corridor.

included: the named class set
clock start, pause and exclusion definitions per class
expedited priority and what funds it
class-level realised-performance auditing
excluded: the price of an expedited class
the queue arithmetic itself
what to do once a specific job is already late

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: measured in-window performance by class diverges from what the class promises

pros.claim: Classes convert an unanswerable question about dates into a repeatable answer the whole bench can give
pros.example: any hand at the counter being able to say a parcel received before the cut-off goes on Tuesday's batch

pros.claim: A stated clock start ends the commonest turnaround argument in trade work
pros.example: an account counting from the day it posted while the parcel sat two days with a carrier, resolved by the received-and-reconciled rule

cons.claim: Classes are coarser than reality and can price or promise a mixed parcel badly
cons.example: a parcel where thirty chains fit the batch class and two rings need stripping, which no single class describes

cons.claim: An expedited class invites accounts to buy priority routinely, which corrodes the schedule it was supposed to protect
cons.example: two accounts both paying for expedition in the same week and neither getting the promised jump

failure_modes: promising a date instead of a class and then owning every carrier delay as a broken promise
offering an expedited class the queue cannot actually honour
never auditing realised performance by class, so a class that always misses keeps being sold
acceptance_tests: each offered class states its clock start, its pause conditions and its exclusions, and is traceable to the capacity model that produced it
realised in-window performance is measured per class at review and any class that misses persistently is restated or withdrawn
revisit_triggers: the capacity model changes
a class misses its window repeatedly across accounts rather than in isolated jobs

nodes.definition: Compose the single document the account relationship runs on, in language a working jeweller reads in two minutes and can find again in a drawer. It names the price basis and its review point; the turnaround classes offered and what starts and pauses the clock; the liability position — the declared value ceiling per parcel, what happens to a piece damaged in process, and the plain statement that no plating job can guarantee an irreplaceable piece against loss, which is why certain items are refused rather than insured; the carrier class for each direction and who books and pays for it; the approval threshold above which the bench stops and asks before proceeding, such as work found to need stripping, stone removal or a rebuilt underplate; the payment terms, statement cadence and what happens when an account passes its aging band; the wear and disclosure clause the account accepts and carries to its own customer; and the classes of work the shop refuses. It is a commercial document setting out mechanisms, not legal drafting: have the wording that matters reviewed by a professional in your jurisdiction before it is used, keep a signed or explicitly acknowledged copy per account rather than a memory of a conversation, and re-issue it when a clause changes instead of relying on the newest verbal version.

included: the clause set and its plain-language form
acknowledgment and re-issue discipline
the refusal-classes and approval-threshold clauses
the disclosure clause the account accepts
excluded: legal drafting or jurisdiction-specific enforceability opinions
the derivation of the price basis
the per-piece intake paperwork inside a parcel

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a dispute, a claim or a rule change shows a clause to be missing, ambiguous or out of date

pros.claim: One acknowledged document removes almost every argument that later starts with the words I thought we agreed
pros.example: a dispute about who pays for return carriage settled by pointing at the clause rather than by memory

pros.claim: Writing the refusal classes into the terms makes a later no a reminder rather than a fresh confrontation
pros.example: declining a parcel containing an irreplaceable inherited locket by citing the clause the account already accepted

cons.claim: A terms sheet can become an unread artefact that neither side follows once the relationship is warm
cons.example: an account that has been sending parcels for a year under terms nobody has looked at since the second month

cons.claim: Small benches lack the appetite and the budget for professional review, and improvised wording carries its own risk
cons.example: a liability clause copied from another trade whose assumptions do not fit custody of customer jewellery

leaving the approval threshold unstated so the bench either stalls constantly or proceeds on irreversible work uninstructed
changing a clause in practice without re-issuing it, so two versions of the truth exist
acceptance_tests: each active account has a dated, acknowledged terms sheet covering price basis, turnaround classes, liability and ceiling, carrier class, approval threshold, payment terms, disclosure clause and refusal classes

revisit_triggers: a dispute exposes a clause that is missing, ambiguous or unworkable in practice

nodes.definition: Treat the arrival of a trade parcel as a custody event with a fixed sequence, because everything later depends on the count being right at this moment. Receive under signature. Before opening, photograph the sealed package as received whenever the packaging is damaged, the seal is disturbed or the weight looks wrong, and note the condition on the carrier's record where the class requires it. Open in a designated clean receiving area away from any chemical work, one parcel at a time, over a lipped tray. Count and identify every piece against the sender's manifest, and reconcile immediately: a short, extra, misdescribed or wrong-piece parcel is reported to the account inside the window the terms name, before any work starts and before pieces are mixed into a batch, because after that the shop is arguing about its own record rather than the sender's. What arrives with no manifest gets one written at receipt and sent to the account for acknowledgment before work begins. Per-piece condition documentation — the photographs of a worn shank, the note on a loose stone or a soft solder joint, the risk acknowledgment for an irreplaceable item — belongs to the intake subdomain and is invoked here rather than redefined; what this unit owns is that the count, the identity of each piece and the exact moment custody transferred are recorded so that responsibility is never a matter of recollection.

included: signature receipt and packaging-condition capture
designated opening area away from chemical work
count and identity reconciliation against the manifest
the discrepancy report window and the no-manifest rule
excluded: per-piece condition photography and heirloom risk acknowledgment, which the intake subdomain owns
assessing whether a piece can be plated to the requested class
the claim process once a loss is established

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a discrepancy or loss event shows the receiving sequence was skipped, rushed or unrecorded

pros.claim: Reconciling before anything is touched keeps a discrepancy the carrier's or sender's question rather than the shop's
pros.example: a parcel found one ring short at opening being reported that morning with photographs of the disturbed seal

pros.claim: A written manifest for manifest-less senders converts an informal habit into a record within one parcel
pros.example: a jeweller who has always sent pieces in a folded envelope acknowledging a receipt list by return message

cons.claim: Full reconciliation of a large mixed parcel costs real bench time before any revenue-earning work begins
cons.example: an hour spent identifying sixty near-identical chain sections against a vague list

cons.claim: A rigid discrepancy window can sour a relationship when the sender simply made an honest packing error
cons.example: a formal shortage notice sent for a piece the account's own bench had kept back and forgotten to strike off

failure_modes: opening a parcel in the plating area or beside a bath, where a dropped piece or a splash becomes two problems at once
starting work on a parcel before reconciling it and losing the ability to say what arrived
accepting a parcel with no manifest and reconstructing the contents later from memory
acceptance_tests: every received parcel has a dated receipt record, a reconciled count against a manifest and, where relevant, packaging-condition images captured before opening
no piece enters a process batch before its parcel has been reconciled and any discrepancy reported inside the terms window
revisit_triggers: a discrepancy is discovered after work has started rather than at opening
an account's packing or manifest practice changes, or a new account arrives with none

nodes.definition: Keep other people's goods identifiable and separated every moment they are inside the shop, because a plating bench is precisely the environment in which small gold-coloured objects lose their identity. Every parcel becomes a lot with an identifier; every piece carries a tag, a numbered bag or a tagged compartment that travels with it through prep, strike, deposit, rinse, dry, cure and inspection; the lot's stage is logged when it moves; goods from different accounts never share an unlabelled tray, a barrel load, a bagging step or a polishing sequence, and near-identical items from different accounts are deliberately scheduled apart rather than sorted by eye afterwards. The day ends with a reconciliation count: pieces at the bench, pieces in process, pieces in the safe and pieces packed for return, all matched against open lots, with any difference chased that evening rather than in the morning. Storage discipline is also safety discipline: customer goods, finished and unfinished, are stored away from chemical storage and never inside a chemical cabinet, and the shop's immovable chemical rule holds over the whole layout the goods live in — cyanide-bearing solutions and acids are never mixed, never stored together and never share a drain. Losses in real shops are mundane: a stone loosened in an ultrasonic bath, an earring left in a rinse tank, a fine chain sunk into another account's barrel load, a repaired piece put back into the wrong bag at the end of a long day.

included: lot and piece identity through every stage
stage logging and account segregation
end-of-day reconciliation count
goods storage separated from chemical storage, under the shop's chemical segregation rules
excluded: process parameters and bath handling procedure
the chemical safety training and hazmat obligations themselves, which the safety specialist owns
per-piece condition documentation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a piece is misplaced, mixed between accounts or found in the wrong lot, or the bench layout and batch practice change

pros.claim: Piece-level identity through every stage makes the end-of-day count meaningful instead of decorative
pros.example: a missing tag traced within the hour to a piece still hanging on a rack rather than discovered a week later at return

pros.claim: Segregating accounts by schedule rather than by eye removes the commonest mix-up in a plating shop
pros.example: two jewellers' near-identical fine curb chains deliberately run on different batch days

cons.claim: Tagging and stage logging cost handling time on exactly the high-volume low-value work whose margin is thinnest
cons.example: individually bagging two hundred trophy findings that would otherwise be tipped into one basket

cons.claim: Tags themselves interfere with the process and must be chosen so they survive or are removed and reapplied at defined points
cons.example: a tag that cannot enter a hot cleaning step forcing a documented hand-off point in the sequence

failure_modes: letting two accounts' similar work share a tray or barrel and sorting by eye afterwards

storing customer goods in or beside chemical storage for convenience during a busy run
acceptance_tests: every piece in the shop is attributable to a lot and an account at any moment, and its current stage is in the log
the end-of-day count reconciles bench, in-process, safe and packed pieces against open lots, with differences chased before close

revisit_triggers: any count discrepancy at end of day, however quickly resolved
a change in bench layout, staffing or batch practice that alters how goods move

nodes.definition: Run a prepared sequence when a parcel is short, damaged, delayed past its tracking or lost, because the first few hours decide both whether cover survives and whether the account stays. Stop and preserve: photograph the packaging and contents exactly as they are, keep every scrap of packaging material, and neither repack nor begin work on a disputed consignment. Notify in the order the terms and the cover conditions require, with the account first so that they are never the last to know — a jeweller who hears about a missing ring from their own customer will not send a third parcel — then the carrier inside its claim window, then whoever administers the shop's cover, recording times, names and reference numbers as you go rather than reconstructing them later. Assemble the evidence set a claim will demand: the manifest, the declared value and its basis, proof of the packaging and service class used, the receipt, tracking and signature record, and the shop's own custody log showing exactly where responsibility sat when the loss occurred. Then hold one honest conversation with the account about remedy, keeping two things separate — what a claim may eventually return, and what the shop chooses to do now for the relationship — and never let an unresolved claim silently stall that account's other work, which is how a recoverable loss turns into a lost account.

included: preserve-and-photograph first steps
notification order and claim windows
the evidence set a claim demands
separating claim outcome from the shop's own remedy decision
excluded: negotiating or interpreting a specific policy wording
legal action and recovery proceedings
in-shop loss of a piece that never left the premises

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a real loss event shows a step in the sequence to be missing, too slow or unsupported by the records kept

pros.claim: A prepared sequence protects the claim at the moment when nobody is thinking clearly
pros.example: packaging kept and photographed before anyone opened the damaged box further, which the carrier later required

pros.claim: Telling the account first preserves the relationship even when the loss is real
pros.example: a jeweller able to speak to their customer the same morning with the facts rather than being ambushed a week later

cons.claim: The evidence a claim requires is often exactly what a casual sender never provided
cons.example: a declared value with no basis and a manifest written by hand with no piece descriptions

cons.claim: Choosing to make the account whole before a claim resolves puts the shop's cash at risk with no certainty of recovery
cons.example: replacing a lost chain immediately and later finding the carrier class capped its liability far below the value

failure_modes: repacking or working on a disputed parcel and destroying the evidence
missing a carrier claim window while deciding internally what to say
going quiet toward the account while the claim runs
acceptance_tests: each loss or shortage event has a dated log of preservation steps, notifications in the required order with reference numbers, and the assembled evidence set
the account was notified before any external party other than the carrier where the class required immediate reporting
revisit_triggers: any loss, shortage or damage event, resolved or not

nodes.definition: Treat a date that is about to be missed as a communication task beginning before the date, not an apology beginning after it. The queue model supplies the early signal — a batch that will not fill, a bath out of service for maintenance or waiting on analysis, a parcel that arrived needing stripping or repair nobody quoted, an approval the account has not answered, a piece failing inspection and needing rework — and the rule is that the account hears it from the bench while they still have options. The call or message carries three things: the revised window with the reason in plain terms and no chemistry lecture, the options the shop can actually offer (release the finished part of the parcel now and follow with the remainder, drop to a different service class, hold for the next batch day, or return the work unworked at no charge), and what the shop is doing so this cause does not repeat. What actually loses accounts is silence: a jeweller who has promised their customer a Friday can absorb a Wednesday warning and cannot absorb a Friday surprise, and the difference between those two conversations is the whole of turnaround reliability as a retention mechanism.

included: early detection signals from the queue
the three contents of the exception message
partial release, reclass, hold and return-unworked options
the no-silence rule
excluded: the technical diagnosis of the bench problem
compensation or credit policy for a missed date
renegotiating the account's standing schedule

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: churn or complaint records show accounts leaving after silent misses rather than after acknowledged ones

pros.claim: An early warning transfers options to the account, which is what a trade partner actually needs from a supplier
pros.example: a jeweller told on Wednesday who chooses partial release so the customer's wedding band goes back on time

pros.claim: Naming the cause and the fix keeps one slip from reading as a pattern
pros.example: explaining that a bath was down for analysis and that the batch day now has reserved capacity for that maintenance

cons.claim: Frequent early warnings advertise instability even when each one is handled well
cons.example: three exception calls in a month leaving an account convinced the bench is unreliable regardless of outcomes

cons.claim: Offering options costs money and disrupts the queue further
cons.example: a partial release requiring an extra packing, an extra carrier booking and a second inspection

failure_modes: waiting until the promised day to make the call
explaining the chemistry instead of giving a revised window and a choice
offering an option the bench cannot actually deliver, turning one slip into two
acceptance_tests: every job that misses its window has a dated record of an exception message sent before the promised date, with the revised window, the options offered and the account's choice
the cause of each slip is recorded in a form the capacity model and the batch schedule can act on
revisit_triggers: slips recur from the same cause across accounts
an account reports learning about a delay from its own customer first

nodes.definition: Adjudicate returned work by cause before discussing money, because the sentence it has gone patchy covers at least five different stories with different owners. Triage against the record. A deposit defect the shop owns looks like poor adhesion, blistering, a dull or off-colour deposit, coverage missing in a recess or a bare edge where the current never reached. Wear that is normal for the class sold is not a fault but a specification mismatch, and it points at how the class was sold rather than at how it was plated — a thin decorative refresh on a daily-worn ring shank returning within months is the class doing exactly what a thin decorative refresh does. A substrate or repair problem present before plating — porosity in a cast piece, a soft solder joint, a previous nickel-free stack, a base metal that was never declared — is the sender's, and is provable only if it was documented at intake. Damage after return, in the account's own workshop or on the customer's hand, is theirs. An expectation the account was never given in writing is the shop's own paperwork failure. The settlement bands follow from the cause: redo at the shop's cost, redo at shared cost where the class was wrong for the use, decline with the evidence and a plain explanation, or route the piece back to the account's own bench. Every claim closes with two outputs: a defect note fed to the process side, because a repeating adhesion pattern is a preparation and bath-condition question for the bench specialists and not a commercial one, and a decision on whether a class description or a terms clause needs rewriting.

included: cause triage across the five classes of claim
settlement bands mapped to cause
the defect note routed to the process side
the terms or class-description review each claim triggers
excluded: diagnosing and correcting the bench cause itself
consumer-facing dispute handling for a walk-in customer
legal dispute resolution

pros.claim: Deciding cause before money keeps settlements consistent between accounts and defensible over time
pros.example: two accounts returning similar chains getting different answers because one was a coverage defect and the other was six months of daily wear on a flash class

cons.example: a pre-existing porous casting that nobody photographed at intake, leaving the shop with no way to prove it

acceptance_tests: every claim record names the cause class, the evidence relied on, the settlement band applied and the defect note or terms action taken

revisit_triggers: the same cause class recurs across accounts or on one account repeatedly

nodes.definition: Keep the record that converts a stream of jobs into an asset. Per account: every parcel with its date, lot identifier, contents, the service and thickness class applied, approvals asked and given, the turnaround class promised and the elapsed time actually achieved, the price basis applied, the carrier class used, and any defect or claim with its cause. Per piece, for anything likely to come back: what it is and how it is recognised, what stack went on it last time, what was masked or removed, what was found wrong before work started, and what the account had been told. This is what lets a re-quote take two minutes instead of a re-discovery, what lets the bench answer the question you did this bangle two years ago, what did you put on it with a fact rather than a guess, and what makes an observed replate interval measurable instead of anecdotal. It is also the evidence base every other unit here reads from: the schedule review, the turnaround audit, the claim triage, the concentration read and the offboarding reconciliation all draw on it. A book with no history is a contact list; a book with history is something a shop can price, insure, hand to a successor or sell.

included: per-parcel job record fields
per-piece recognition and stack history
the record as evidence base for review, audit, triage and reconciliation
retention so the record outlives the owner's memory
excluded: process logs of bath parameters and analysis, which the bench specialists keep
accounting ledgers and tax records
the account's own customer records

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a question the book must answer cannot be answered from the fields currently recorded

pros.claim: History collapses re-quoting effort and removes the guesswork on returning pieces
pros.example: a returning bangle re-quoted from the recorded class and area of its last visit rather than re-measured and re-argued

pros.claim: Only a real history can produce observed replate intervals, which is the difference between forecasting and guessing
pros.example: an account's fashion stock showing a consistent return pattern by piece class across two years of records

cons.example: a three-hundred-piece findings batch recorded only at lot level, which is the right trade but leaves a gap

cons.example: an account asking about a piece from three years ago that would take an afternoon to find

letting the record live in one person's head or one person's notebook
acceptance_tests: for any completed parcel the record shows date, lot, contents, class applied, approvals, promised and achieved turnaround, price basis and any defect or claim

nodes.definition: Understand where the repeat actually comes from, because it is a property of the product rather than a triumph of marketing: plated gold is a surface, surfaces wear, and every piece that leaves this bench is a future job whose timing is governed by mechanism. What moves the interval is the deposit class and thickness applied, the underplate and barrier beneath it, the use class of the piece — a daily-worn ring shank, a bracelet clasp and a watch bezel abrade in ways an earring or a pendant never will — and the wearer's own chemistry, habits and what they clean it with. That mechanism supports a forecast built from the shop's own evidence: the installed base plated per account, and the return intervals actually observed by piece class in the job history. It does not support a promise. A statement that this will last a given number of years is a claim the shop cannot make and must not let an account make on its behalf; the honest form is the mechanism, the class that was applied, and the intervals this shop has measured, offered as an expectation with its basis attached. Handled this way the replate cycle becomes a demand engine the account welcomes rather than a complaint queue: a jeweller who understands that a class of their stock comes back can plan a refresh drive, price for it, and stop being surprised by it.

included: the mechanism that moves the replate interval
installed base and observed-interval forecasting from own history
the expectation-not-guarantee form of every statement
planning refresh demand with an account
excluded: stating any wear-life figure as a general fact
wear testing methods and thickness verification, which the quality side owns
the price of a replate

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: accumulated return records shift the observed interval distribution for a piece or deposit class

pros.claim: Forecasting from installed base and observed intervals gives the bench a demand picture nobody else in the trade has
pros.example: knowing which account's stock class is due for a refresh season and offering a batch day before they ask
