pros.example: a jeweller told at the outset that a flash class on a daily-worn shank is a maintenance cycle, not a permanent finish

cons.claim: Intervals vary so widely by wearer that any average is weak evidence for an individual piece
cons.example: two identical chains from the same batch returning a year apart because of who wore them and how

cons.claim: The honest form disappoints an account that wants a durability number to sell against a competitor's claim
cons.example: a reseller pressing for a lifetime finish claim the shop will not supply

failure_modes: converting an observed interval into a guarantee because an account asked twice
forecasting demand from ambition rather than from the installed base actually plated
treating every return as a defect, which hides real defects among normal cycle work
acceptance_tests: every wear or interval statement to an account names its basis — the mechanism plus intervals observed in this shop's records — and is labelled an expectation rather than a guarantee
the demand forecast is traceable to installed base and observed return intervals in the job history rather than to a target
revisit_triggers: observed return intervals diverge from the working expectation for a piece class
a change in deposit class, underplate practice or topcoat use alters the wear behaviour of what the shop ships

nodes.definition: Run the money side of an account with the same discipline as the custody side, since a book of loyal accounts that pay late is a cash-flow trap rather than an asset. Invoice against the job record so every line traces back to a lot, a class and a date; issue statements on a stated cadence rather than when cash gets tight, because irregular chasing trains accounts to wait; age the balances so that a slow account is visible while it is merely slow rather than after it is a problem; and set a per-account exposure limit that counts two things together — the unpaid invoices and the value of that account's goods currently sitting in the shop, because the shop is financing both at once. The terms sheet already states what happens when an account passes its limit or its aging band, so the escalation is a sequence rather than a mood: a reminder, a call, a work-stop on new parcels, completion and hold of work in progress, return of goods on settlement, then a decision about offboarding. Holding an account's goods against a debt is a step with legal implications that vary by jurisdiction and must not be improvised — take proper advice before doing it, and put whatever is agreed into the terms in advance. These are commercial mechanisms only: specific credit, tax and recovery decisions belong with the shop's own accountant and adviser.

included: invoicing traceable to the job record
statement cadence and aging bands
exposure limit combining receivables and goods on premises
the escalation sequence to work-stop and hold
excluded: personalised credit, tax or debt-recovery advice
the legal mechanics of retaining goods against a debt in any jurisdiction
pricing and cost derivation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: aging trends, a bad debt, or a change in the terms or the applicable rules on holding goods

pros.claim: Counting goods on premises inside the exposure limit reveals the true amount the shop has riding on one account
pros.example: an account inside its invoice limit while holding a tray of its unfinished parcels worth several times that limit

pros.claim: A stated escalation sequence makes chasing routine rather than personal, so it actually happens
pros.example: a work-stop triggered by an aging band that the account was told about at the second reminder, not sprung on them

cons.claim: Enforcing a work-stop on a long-standing account risks a relationship the book depends on
cons.example: pausing new parcels from the shop's largest jeweller during their busiest fortnight

cons.claim: Ledger discipline consumes owner time that a small bench would rather spend at the bench
cons.example: a statement run and aging review that costs half a day a month at exactly the busiest point

failure_modes: invoicing from memory rather than from the job record, so lines cannot be defended when queried
measuring exposure on invoices alone and ignoring the value of goods held
letting a favourite account age indefinitely because the conversation is uncomfortable
acceptance_tests: every invoice line traces to a lot and a class in the job record, and statements are issued on the stated cadence
each account has an exposure limit that includes goods on premises, and any breach has a recorded escalation step rather than an exception
revisit_triggers: an account's aging trend deteriorates for two consecutive periods
the terms sheet payment clauses change or a jurisdiction rule affecting them changes

nodes.definition: Read the book as a portfolio rather than as a set of friendships. Per account, the health signals are cadence measured against that account's own baseline rather than against other accounts, mix drift — a jeweller who used to send heavy replates now sending only flash refreshes is telling you something about their own trade or about your price — parcel size drift, claim and rework rate, payment aging trend, and how quickly approvals come back. A quiet account is usually a leaving account, and the drift is visible a cycle or two before the loss, which is the only window in which anything can be done about it. Across the book, the number that matters is concentration: what share of revenue and of committed bench hours sits with one account or one class of account, and what the week looks like if that account stops tomorrow. Concentration is not automatically a fault — a well-run repair chain can be worth building capacity around, and pretending otherwise leaves capacity idle — but it must be a decision with a stated tolerance, a watch on that account's own health, and a deliberate effort to broaden the base while the large account is still happy rather than in the month after it leaves.

included: per-account drift and health signals against own baseline
concentration by revenue and by committed bench hours
a stated concentration tolerance and the watch it implies
the early window for intervention on a drifting account
excluded: the intervention conversation itself, which is a sales matter
the decision to end an account
capacity modelling

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: churn outcomes show which drift signals actually preceded losses and which were seasonal noise

pros.claim: Baseline-relative cadence catches the quiet exit while there is still time to ask why
pros.example: an account whose fortnightly parcels became monthly being called before the third missed cycle

pros.claim: A stated concentration tolerance turns a hidden dependency into a managed one
pros.example: a chain account at a large share of bench hours triggering a deliberate push for two mid-sized jewellers

cons.claim: Trade cadence is naturally lumpy and seasonal, so drift signals produce false alarms
cons.example: a quiet six weeks after an account's own stocktake being read as churn

cons.claim: Deliberately capping a good account's share can leave capacity unfilled and margin unearned
cons.example: declining extra volume from a reliable chain and then running a half-empty batch day

failure_modes: measuring cadence against the book average instead of the account's own baseline
noticing concentration only when the large account leaves
reading health from revenue alone while claim rate and approval responsiveness were signalling first
acceptance_tests: each account has a baseline and a current read on cadence, mix, claim rate and aging, reviewed on the book cadence
the book's concentration by revenue and by committed bench hours is stated with a tolerance and a dated decision
revisit_triggers: an account crosses its drift thresholds on cadence, mix or claim rate
concentration passes the stated tolerance in either direction

nodes.definition: Grow the book the way trade books actually grow, which is sideways through the people already in it. The mechanism is an introduction between peers who share a customer type but not a customer — one jeweller telling another who does their plating — and it fires most reliably at two moments: after a job that went visibly right, especially a rescue or a difficult piece, and after a job the bench honestly refused with a clear explanation, because a supplier who says no credibly is worth recommending. Ask at those moments and ask specifically: an introduction to a named peer beats tell your friends by a wide margin. Then make the introduction easy to act on with something the peer can hold — a card, a single page saying what the bench does, what it refuses and what its turnaround classes are, and a sample set showing finish classes side by side so a jeweller can see the difference between a refresh and a wear-duty replate. Reciprocity is the other half: work declined because it is outside this bench's competence should go somewhere by name, and the bench that receives it remembers who sent it. The line that is never crossed is that no referral or reciprocal arrangement funds a message that misleads an end consumer about what a plated finish is, and no introduction is warm enough to justify taking on an account whose selling practice the shop would not want its name attached to.

included: the two moments an introduction fires
the specific named-peer ask
the carry-away artefacts including a finish-class sample set
reciprocal referral of refused work and the honesty line
excluded: consumer-facing marketing and advertising
paying for placement or commission structures with end-consumer claims attached
qualification of the referred prospect, which the qualification unit owns

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: logged referral sources and outcomes show which moment and which ask actually produce accounts

pros.claim: Referred accounts arrive pre-qualified on the dimension that matters most, which is whether they can work with written terms and honest classes
pros.example: a jeweller introduced by an existing account already expecting the wear language on the returned ticket

pros.claim: A finish-class sample set does the explaining that words fail at, and travels between benches
pros.example: a peer seeing a refreshed shank next to a wear-duty replate and understanding the price difference immediately

cons.claim: Referral growth is slow, lumpy and cannot be turned on when the book has a hole in it
cons.example: a quiet quarter after an account leaves that no amount of asking fills in time

cons.claim: A referral creates social pressure to accept an account that qualification would decline
cons.example: a good account's friend arriving with parcels above the shop's ceiling and an expectation of a favour

failure_modes: asking vaguely and receiving nothing, rather than asking for one named introduction
letting a warm introduction bypass qualification and the terms sheet
entering a reciprocal arrangement whose downstream selling message the shop cannot stand behind
acceptance_tests: referral introductions are logged with their source and outcome, and every referred prospect goes through the same qualification and terms process as a cold one
no referral or reciprocal arrangement is entered where the receiving party's consumer-facing claims about plated finishes cannot be verified as honest
revisit_triggers: referred accounts fail qualification more often than cold ones
a referral partner is found making unsupported claims about plated work

nodes.definition: End an account deliberately when it should end, and end it clean. The honest grounds are few: chronic losses on work that reconciliation shows cannot be priced into profitability at any level the account will accept; payment behaviour that has run the full escalation sequence without changing; risk the shop cannot carry, meaning parcel values or item types that sit outside the ceiling and the refusal criteria; abusive or dishonest conduct; and the one owners avoid longest, an account that repeatedly pressures the bench to misrepresent what it deposited or to soften the wear language reaching a consumer. The closing sequence is mechanical and should be dull: accept no new work, finish or return work in progress by agreement, reconcile every open lot piece by piece against its manifest, return the goods by an agreed carrier class with signature and a receipt, issue and settle the final statement, and archive rather than delete the account's job history, because a piece from that account can still walk back in through another door and its history is still the right answer. Say the reason once, plainly, without a lecture and without a list of grievances, and leave the door open where the reason is commercial rather than ethical — a shop that cannot afford an account this year may want it in two.

included: the grounds for ending an account
the closing sequence and final reconciliation
history archiving after closure
how the reason is delivered
excluded: debt recovery action and legal process
refusing an individual piece within a continuing account
the health signals that led to the decision

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a closure that produced a dispute, an unreturned piece or an unsettled balance

pros.claim: A mechanical closing sequence prevents the loose ends that turn an ending into a dispute
pros.example: every open lot reconciled and signed for on return, so no piece is unaccounted for a month later

pros.claim: Ending an account on ethical grounds protects the disclosure discipline the whole book depends on
pros.example: closing a reseller that kept asking for invoices without the word plated after two documented refusals

cons.claim: Closing an account removes revenue immediately while the replacement is slow and uncertain
cons.example: a loss-making but high-volume account whose exit empties two batch days a month

cons.claim: Word travels in a small trade, and even a clean ending can be retold badly by the other side
cons.example: a closed account describing a work-stop for non-payment as unreliability to its peers

failure_modes: drifting out of an account by becoming slow and unresponsive instead of saying so
closing while lots are still open or the final statement is unsettled
deleting the history and losing the ability to answer for work already done
acceptance_tests: at closure every open lot is reconciled and returned under signature, the final statement is issued, and the reason and date are recorded in the account file
the account's job history is archived and remains retrievable for work the shop performed
revisit_triggers: a closed account asks to return, or a piece from it comes back through another route
closures cluster around one cause, which points at a term, a class or a qualification gap

nodes.definition: Put the whole book on a review cadence so it is steered rather than merely accumulated, and read the same evidence every time so that changes mean something. The review looks at realised turnaround by class against the classes promised; claim and rework rate by account and by cause; reconciled profitability by account and by service class, taken from job costing rather than from a feeling about who is pleasant; cadence, mix and concentration trends; the replate intervals the accumulated history now shows; and the accounts currently on watch. It produces decisions rather than observations: schedules re-derived, classes retired or added, capacity reallocated between accounts and channels, one account promoted to a standing batch day, another moved to prepay or a capped parcel value, one offboarded, and a stated target for where the next accounts should come from. The review is also the place where the terms sheet and the class descriptions get edited from experience rather than from theory, and where the shop is obliged to admit the uncomfortable thing — a promise class that keeps being missed is a promise the shop should stop making, and a saving that funds a trade level but never actually occurs is a discount with no basis.

included: the fixed evidence set read at every review
decisions the review must produce
editing terms and class descriptions from experience
the target for where new accounts come from
excluded: the individual account conversations that follow
process and quality review of the bench itself
annual accounts and tax reporting

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the review's decisions are not implemented, or the evidence set fails to surface a problem the book later pays for

pros.claim: A fixed evidence set makes reviews comparable, so trends emerge instead of impressions
pros.example: three consecutive reviews showing the same class missing its window, which no single month made obvious

pros.claim: Requiring decisions rather than observations stops the review becoming a ritual
pros.example: a review that ends with one schedule re-derived, one class withdrawn and one account moved to prepay

cons.claim: A small bench genuinely struggles to protect review time against the queue
cons.example: the review sliding for two quarters while a below-cost schedule keeps being honoured

cons.claim: Reviewing on a fixed cadence can be too slow for a fast-moving problem
cons.example: a carrier terms change that needed action in a week rather than at the next quarterly review

failure_modes: reviewing revenue only and never realised turnaround, claim causes or reconciled profitability
producing observations with no owner and no date, so nothing changes
letting the review replace the event-driven triggers that must fire immediately
acceptance_tests: each review records the full evidence set and produces dated decisions with an owner, including at least the schedule, class and watch-list outcomes
decisions from the previous review are checked for completion before new ones are made
revisit_triggers: an event-driven trigger fires that cannot wait for the next scheduled review
two consecutive reviews produce no decisions, which means the evidence set or the cadence is wrong

edges.why_related: the channel separation applies the charter's custodial and disclosure premises to the two kinds of customer the bench serves
partner classes are only meaningful once trade work has been distinguished from walk-in work
the duty to send the plated character onward with the goods is one of the charter's founding premises made operational
qualification tests a specific prospect against the expectations and risks its class carries
no standing schedule is set before the account has been qualified and at least one parcel reconciled
the ceiling for an account is set from the work mix and parcel values qualification established
the declared value decides which movement classes can legitimately carry the parcel at all
the charter's rule that promises must be derivable from capability is what makes the queue model mandatory rather than optional
each named class is a window the queue arithmetic can actually support, not a marketing choice
the terms sheet publishes the classes with their clock start, pause conditions and exclusions
the terms sheet names the price basis this account works from and its review point
the receiving sequence must satisfy the reporting, signature and condition-capture conditions the chosen carrier class requires
lots and piece identities that the in-shop ledger tracks are created at reconciliation
the job record is posted from the lot, stage and inspection entries the custody ledger produced
installed base and observed return intervals can only be read out of a real job history
cadence, mix, claim-rate and concentration reads are computed from the per-account job record
the wear and disclosure clause is a mandatory term the account must accept, not an optional appendix
a parcel whose declared value exceeds the ceiling is held, split or refused rather than routinely received and opened
the liability position, approval threshold and class descriptions in the terms bound what any claim settlement can be
a claim can only be adjudicated on cause where the custody and stage record shows what happened to the piece and when
replate demand may be described by mechanism and observed intervals but never converted into a wear-life guarantee
terms are acknowledged before the first parcel moves, so the discrepancy window and liability position already exist when goods arrive
the class chosen determines the claim window, the evidence required and the order in which a loss must be reported
offboarding on payment grounds only follows a completed escalation sequence, and closure requires a final reconciled statement
accounts leave after silent misses far more than after acknowledged ones, so exception behaviour drives the churn signal
the installed base returning for renewal creates predictable load the capacity plan must reserve for
a rising claim rate on an account is one of the earliest precursors of its departure
introductions from existing accounts are what actually refills the prospect pool, and they arrive skewed toward the classes already in the book
reconciled jobs tell the review whether the savings that fund an account's level actually occurred
a claim cause that recurs is evidence that a clause or a class description needs rewriting rather than re-arguing
a class that generates exception calls repeatedly is a promise the shop should restate or withdraw
every loss or near-loss re-ranks the movement classes and exposes a condition the shop was not meeting
what the book learns about which accounts worked changes which checks qualification applies to the next prospect
the volume that justifies a keener trade level is exactly the volume that builds dangerous concentration in one account
edges.resolution_rule: grant the level on the named saving but hold it inside the stated concentration tolerance; if the account would exceed the tolerance, cap the committed share and broaden the base rather than deepen the discount

edges.why_related: hitting a promised window pushes against tagging, stage logging, segregation and the end-of-day count, which all cost handling time
edges.resolution_rule: custody and segregation discipline never yields to a date; if the class cannot be met with the discipline intact, the date moves and the account is told early

edges.why_related: the accounts most worth keeping are the ones most likely to ask for consolidated parcels above the ceiling
edges.resolution_rule: the ceiling holds regardless of account importance; split the consignment, change the movement class or decline the parcel, and record the decision rather than making an exception

edges.why_related: an account wanting a cheap class described as something more valuable is asking the shop to buy volume with its honesty
edges.resolution_rule: disclosure wins absolutely: the documentation states the class and deposit actually applied, and an account that persists is refused and offboarded rather than accommodated at any price

edges.why_related: enforcing a work-stop on an overdue account collides with the referral goodwill that account generates
edges.resolution_rule: run the written escalation sequence on schedule and keep the conversation warm and specific; goodwill may change the tone and the timing within the terms, never the existence of the limit

edges.why_related: both are loss-event disciplines that decide cause from a preserved record before money is discussed, and both close by feeding the cause back into a class or a term

conflict_axes.name: promise_speed_vs_bench_reality
conflict_axes.description: Trade accounts buy turnaround, and the pressure to answer a date with the answer the account wants collides with what the queue, the batch cadence and the fixed sequence time can actually support.
poles: promise the date the account asks for
promise only what the queue model supports
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: quote the class the capacity model supports, name the clock start, and buy goodwill with early exception warnings rather than with optimistic dates

conflict_axes.name: trade_level_keenness_vs_cost_recovery
conflict_axes.description: A keener standing schedule wins and holds accounts, while every point of it must come out of a saving that genuinely occurs rather than out of margin the bench cannot spare.
poles: price to win and hold the account
price only to identified savings and reconciled cost
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: grant a level only against a named saving, review it against reconciled job costs, and withdraw or restructure it when the saving stops occurring

conflict_axes.name: account_accommodation_vs_disclosure_duty
conflict_axes.description: Accounts sometimes want documentation, wording or silence that would let a plated piece read as solid gold or as more than it is, and accommodating them is the fastest way to lose the shop's standing.
poles: keep the account happy
keep the disclosure intact
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: disclosure dominates without exception; state the class and deposit applied, refuse the request in writing, and offboard the account if it persists

conflict_axes.name: growth_of_a_big_account_vs_concentration_risk
conflict_axes.description: Building capacity around a large reliable account is efficient and profitable right up to the moment that account leaves, moves its work in-house or is bought.
poles: build capacity around the big account
cap its share and broaden the base
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: state a concentration tolerance, watch that account's own health signals, and spend the good period recruiting mid-sized accounts rather than the period after it leaves

conflict_axes.name: parcel_convenience_vs_liability_ceiling
conflict_axes.description: Consolidated parcels and casual carrier choices are cheaper and easier for everyone, and they are exactly what puts uncovered value on a van or an unwatched bench.
poles: accept the parcel as the account wants to send it
hold the ceiling and the movement class
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold the ceiling and the class conditions, split or reclass the consignment, and record the decision so it is a rule rather than a mood

conflict_axes.name: throughput_pressure_vs_custody_and_safety_discipline
conflict_axes.description: Tagging, segregating, stage logging, counting out at night and keeping goods away from chemical storage all cost time on precisely the busiest days.
poles: push the parcels through
keep every piece attributable and safely stored
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: custody, segregation and the chemical storage rules never yield to throughput; reduce work accepted rather than the discipline applied

conflict_axes.name: goodwill_redo_vs_evidence_based_settlement
conflict_axes.description: Redoing any returned job keeps the peace and teaches accounts to buy the wrong class, while an evidence-based decline is correct and costs relationship warmth at the worst moment.
poles: redo whatever comes back
settle strictly on documented cause
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: triage cause first from the record, apply the settlement band the cause dictates, and treat any goodwill redo as an explicit, logged exception with a class-description fix attached

conflict_axes.name: relationship_patience_vs_credit_exposure
conflict_axes.description: Long-standing accounts are given time to pay because the relationship matters, and the shop is simultaneously financing their receivables and holding their goods.
poles: extend patience to keep the account
enforce the limit and the escalation
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: run the written escalation on schedule with a limit that counts goods on premises as well as invoices; adjust tone freely, never the limit

conflict_axes.name: record_keeping_effort_vs_bench_time
conflict_axes.description: Every record that makes the book durable — manifests, tags, stage logs, job history, claim causes — is time not spent plating, and the pressure to thin it is strongest on the highest-count lowest-value work.
poles: record everything per piece
protect bench hours
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: scale granularity to value and risk — piece-level for identifiable and high-value items, lot-level for bulk findings — but never below the level at which the count and the account attribution stay provable

conflict_axes.name: forecast_usefulness_vs_wear_life_honesty
conflict_axes.description: Accounts want a durability figure they can sell against, and the shop can honestly offer only a mechanism plus the return intervals it has actually observed.
poles: give the account a number to sell with
state only the mechanism and observed intervals
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: supply the mechanism, the class applied and the shop's own observed intervals labelled as an expectation with its basis; never issue a wear-life guarantee and never let an account attribute one to the shop

edge_cases.description: A parcel arrives with the outer packaging intact but one ring short against the manifest, and the account insists it was packed
edge_cases.mitigation: stop, photograph the packaging and contents as found, do not begin work on any piece from that parcel, report inside the terms window with the images and the reconciled count, and open the carrier notification in parallel so no claim window is lost while the two shops compare notes

edge_cases.description: An account books a high-value consignment on a general parcel courier whose terms exclude jewellery, and it is already in transit
edge_cases.trigger: inbound parcel moving on a class that does not cover the commodity
edge_cases.mitigation: receive and reconcile as normal but record the exposure explicitly, tell the account the class carried no effective cover for the goods, and fix the inbound class in the terms before the next parcel rather than after the loss

edge_cases.description: An account asks for an invoice that omits the word plated, or wants a base-metal line described with a marking term reserved for other substrates
edge_cases.trigger: a request to soften or remove disclosure language on trade documentation
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse in writing, restate what was deposited and on what substrate, point the account to the current marking rules in its own market to verify what it may claim, log the request in the account file, and treat repetition as an offboarding ground

edge_cases.description: An irreplaceable inherited piece is discovered inside a routine trade parcel with no special flag from the account
edge_cases.trigger: a piece whose loss no price could answer arrives inside ordinary batch work
edge_cases.mitigation: quarantine the piece before it joins any batch, call the account for its provenance and instruction, apply the shop's refusal criteria and the intake subdomain's risk-acknowledgment path if it proceeds, and remind the account of the flagging duty in the terms

edge_cases.description: A stone is found loose or lost during cleaning of a trade piece that arrived with no per-piece condition record
edge_cases.trigger: damage or loss on the bench with no documented pre-existing condition
edge_cases.mitigation: stop work on the lot, photograph the piece and the equipment state, log the stage where it happened, tell the account the same day, and accept that without an intake record the shop will carry the outcome — then close the gap by routing stone-set pieces through the intake documentation path before cleaning

edge_cases.description: Two accounts send near-identical fine chains in the same week and the pieces are staged together on the same tray beside the plating line
edge_cases.trigger: similar goods from different accounts converging in one batch window
edge_cases.mitigation: schedule the two lots onto different runs, keep each in a tagged bag rather than a shared tray, stage them in the designated goods area away from chemical storage and open baths, and reconcile both lots at the end of day before either is packed

edge_cases.description: A bath is taken out of service mid-week for maintenance or is waiting on analysis, and three accounts have parcels promised for that batch day
edge_cases.trigger: capacity loss after commitments are made
edge_cases.mitigation: re-run the queue that morning, message every affected account before the promised day with a revised window and options, prioritise by what each account has itself promised its customer rather than by account size, and record the cause so the capacity model reserves for it

edge_cases.description: An account wants a written wear-life guarantee in the terms so it can close a retail sale against a competitor's durability claim
edge_cases.trigger: pressure to convert an observed interval into a promise
edge_cases.mitigation: decline the guarantee, supply instead the class applied, the mechanism that moves the interval and the intervals this shop has observed, labelled as an expectation with its basis, and offer a replate-cycle arrangement that makes the return a planned service rather than a broken promise

edge_cases.description: The largest account passes its aging band in the same week that a full tray of its unfinished goods sits in the shop
edge_cases.trigger: receivable exposure and goods-on-premises exposure peak together
edge_cases.mitigation: run the written escalation, accept no new parcels, finish and hold work in progress, and return the account's goods on settlement under the terms already agreed rather than improvising a retention decision that varies by jurisdiction

edge_cases.description: A fashion brand sends a base-metal skin-contact production run and asks the shop to confirm it will be compliant for sale
edge_cases.trigger: a compliance question about skin contact, nickel release or marking arriving as a commercial request
edge_cases.mitigation: state what the shop will deposit and on what declared substrate, name nickel release and marking as obligation classes the brand must verify against current rules in its selling market, route the testing question to the quality and compliance side, and never issue a compliance confirmation the shop is not qualified to give

edge_cases.description: A warm referral arrives from the book's best account, and the prospect's own listings describe plated stock in language implying solid gold
edge_cases.trigger: a referred prospect whose selling practice fails the honesty check
edge_cases.mitigation: run the same qualification as for a cold prospect, raise the listing language directly, open only if it is corrected and the disclosure clause is accepted, and tell the referring account plainly why if it is declined

edge_cases.description: A steady account goes quiet for two cycles with no complaint, no claim and no explanation
edge_cases.trigger: cadence drop against the account's own baseline with no adverse event
edge_cases.mitigation: call before the third missed cycle, check the job history for a slipped date, a claim or a price change that preceded the drop, distinguish seasonal lull from churn using that account's own baseline, and decide deliberately whether to invest, wean or let it go

workflow.action: Write the trade-book charter and separate the channels
workflow.description: Fix the custodial-exposure premise, the capability-derived-promise rule, the disclosure premise and the write-it-down rule, and label how trade work differs from walk-in work
workflow.artifact: trade book charter with channel definitions
workflow.gate: all four premises are written in terms a bench hand can apply, and every job ticket format carries a channel label

workflow.action: Fix the disclosure that travels with the goods
workflow.description: Define the class and deposit language that must appear on every ticket and invoice, and the refusal position on misrepresentation and on blessing marking claims
workflow.gate: the documentation states service class, deposit in plain words, substrate and plated-surface statement, and asserts no marking claim

workflow.description: Place the prospect in its partner class, run the identity, capability, expectation and payment checks, and reach an open, restricted or decline verdict with a sample parcel where useful
workflow.gate: the verdict is dated and reasoned, and no standing schedule is granted before a reconciled first parcel

workflow.description: Count attended hours, session capacity, fixed sequence time and committed load to produce realistic completion windows
workflow.artifact: capacity and queue model with current commitments
workflow.gate: the model yields a window rather than a date and reserves time for maintenance, analysis and inspection

workflow.description: Convert the queue arithmetic into named classes with clock start, pause conditions and exclusions
workflow.gate: each class traces to the capacity model and states what starts, pauses and excludes it

workflow.action: Set the value ceilings and the movement classes
workflow.description: Write the per-parcel and on-premises ceilings from the shop's own cover and security documents, and choose the inbound and outbound carrier classes against the three selection questions
workflow.artifact: ceiling and carrier-class schedule per account
workflow.gate: ceilings are traceable to policy and carrier documents, and each direction has a class whose conditions the shop can actually meet

workflow.description: Name the standing schedule, the savings that fund it, the metal-basis treatment and the review point
workflow.gate: every level is tied to a named saving and a dated review point, with the metal-basis treatment stated

workflow.action: Issue and have the terms sheet acknowledged
workflow.description: Assemble price basis, turnaround classes, liability and ceiling, carrier class, approval threshold, payment terms, disclosure clause and refusal classes into one readable document
workflow.artifact: signed or acknowledged account terms sheet
workflow.gate: a dated acknowledgment exists before the first parcel is accepted, and every clause has a named owner in the shop

workflow.action: Receive and reconcile the first parcel
workflow.description: Sign for it, capture packaging condition where warranted, open in the designated area, count and identify against the manifest and report any discrepancy inside the window
workflow.gate: no piece enters a batch before the parcel is reconciled and any discrepancy is reported

workflow.action: Run custody, delivery and exception handling through the job
workflow.description: Tag and log every piece by stage, segregate accounts, count out at end of day, and message the account before any promised window is missed
workflow.artifact: custody ledger with stage log and exception messages
workflow.gate: every piece is attributable to a lot at any moment, the daily count reconciles, and any slip was communicated before its date

workflow.action: Post the job to history and invoice against it
workflow.description: Record class applied, approvals, promised and achieved turnaround, price basis, carrier class and any defect at return, then invoice from that record and age the balance
workflow.artifact: posted job record and invoice traceable to the lot
workflow.gate: the record is posted at return rather than at month end and every invoice line traces to a lot and a class

workflow.action: Review the book and decide grow, wean or end
workflow.description: Read realised turnaround by class, claim causes, reconciled profitability, cadence, concentration and observed replate intervals, and produce dated decisions
workflow.artifact: book review with dated decisions and owners
workflow.gate: the previous review's decisions are checked for completion and this review produces schedule, class and watch-list outcomes with owners

priority_rationale: The charter, the channel separation and the disclosure duty come first because every later decision — who is taken on, what is promised, what leaves with the goods — is a consequence of them; qualification, the price basis, the value ceiling and the carrier classes come next because they are the inputs the terms sheet composes, and the terms sheet must exist before any parcel moves; capacity and the turnaround classes sit alongside them because a promise that is not derived from queue arithmetic is the fastest way to lose a book; the custody chain from parcel receipt through stage logging to the posted job record follows, because everything downstream is evidence-dependent and evidence can only be created while the goods are in hand; and the recurring layer — replate demand, ledger discipline, account health and concentration, referral, offboarding and the book review — comes last because each of them reads the accumulated record rather than creating it.

dominance_rules.rule: Honest disclosure of the plated character dominates every account accommodation, price and volume consideration
dominance_rules.rationale: the account resells to a consumer who must never be told a plated surface is solid gold, and one accommodation of that kind contaminates the shop's standing with every other account
dominance_rules.trigger: an account asks for documentation, wording or silence that would let the work read as solid gold or as a class it is not
dominance_rules.action: refuse in writing, restate the class and deposit actually applied, log the request, and offboard the account if it persists

dominance_rules.rule: Chemical safety and segregation rules dominate any deadline, parcel flow or storage convenience
dominance_rules.rationale: the shop's hazard obligations are fixed by its jurisdiction and its chemistry, not by its order book, and the hard lines are not negotiable at any level of urgency
dominance_rules.trigger: a busy run tempts the bench to open, stage or store goods in the chemical area, or to shortcut segregation, storage or handling rules
dominance_rules.action: keep goods and chemicals separate, hold the rule that cyanide-bearing solutions and acids are never mixed, never stored together and never share a drain, verify the workplace and hazmat rules that apply in your jurisdiction, and move the date instead of the rule

dominance_rules.rationale: the shop holds property it does not own, and an untraceable piece is a loss no amount of finished work compensates
dominance_rules.trigger: tagging, stage logging, segregation or the end-of-day count is under time pressure
dominance_rules.action: accept less work or move the promise; never run a batch whose pieces cannot be attributed to their lot and account

dominance_rules.rule: The declared value ceiling dominates account importance and parcel convenience
dominance_rules.rationale: a ceiling that bends for the biggest account is not a ceiling, and the exposure it was written to bound is exactly the exposure that account creates
dominance_rules.trigger: a parcel or an on-premises aggregate would exceed a written ceiling
dominance_rules.action: split the consignment, change the movement class, hold it sealed, or decline it, and record the decision in the account file

dominance_rules.rule: Capability-derived promises dominate the demand for a date
dominance_rules.rationale: a trade account buys repeatability, and a fast broken promise costs more than a slower honest one
dominance_rules.trigger: an account presses for a date the queue model does not support
dominance_rules.action: offer the class the model supports, or offer expedition at the price of the disruption it causes, and never confirm a date the queue cannot produce

dominance_rules.rationale: accounts survive acknowledged misses and leave after silent ones, because a warned account still has options with its own customer
dominance_rules.trigger: any signal that a promised window will be missed
dominance_rules.action: message the account before the promised date with the revised window, the options and the fix

dominance_rules.rule: Refusal criteria for irreplaceable items dominate the value of the account sending them
dominance_rules.rationale: no job is worth an irreplaceable loss, and no ceiling or cover restores a piece that cannot be replaced
dominance_rules.trigger: an irreplaceable or unflagged heirloom piece appears in a trade parcel
dominance_rules.action: quarantine it, call the account, and refuse or proceed only through the documented risk-acknowledgment path the intake subdomain defines

dominance_rules.rule: Documented evidence dominates recollection in any claim or discrepancy
dominance_rules.rationale: memory is worthless against a manifest, a photograph and a stage log, and the party without records carries the outcome
dominance_rules.trigger: a claim, shortage or damage dispute arises
dominance_rules.action: triage on the manifest, images, custody log and terms; where the record does not exist, accept the outcome and fix the record-keeping gap rather than arguing

dominance_rules.rule: Cost recovery dominates volume ambition when a trade level is set or defended
dominance_rules.rationale: a level unfunded by a real saving loses money on every parcel and loses more as volume grows
dominance_rules.trigger: a schedule is proposed or defended on the promise of future volume
dominance_rules.action: require the named saving and the reconciled cost check; restructure or withdraw the level rather than hoping volume repairs it

dominance_rules.rule: Written and acknowledged terms dominate verbal arrangements
dominance_rules.rationale: two people remembering a corridor conversation differently is the origin of most trade disputes
dominance_rules.trigger: an operating rule is agreed, changed or disputed with an account
dominance_rules.action: re-issue the clause, obtain acknowledgment, and operate from the issued version rather than the newest conversation

dominance_rules.rule: The bench cause dominates the commercial settlement in a claim
dominance_rules.rationale: paying a credit and moving on leaves the defect in the process to be paid for again
dominance_rules.trigger: any claim closes, whatever the settlement
dominance_rules.action: route the cause note to the process side for preparation and bath-condition review and record whether a class description or term needs rewriting

anti_rework_rules.rule: Derive the capacity and queue model before publishing any turnaround class
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a promise class the bench cannot honour, which has to be withdrawn after it has already broken dates across several accounts

anti_rework_rules.rule: Agree the value ceiling and the carrier class for both directions before the first parcel ships
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering after a loss that the inbound class excluded the commodity or that the parcel was above the cap

anti_rework_rules.rule: Get the terms sheet acknowledged before accepting work, not after the first dispute
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reconstructing liability, approval thresholds and disclosure duties from memory in the middle of an argument

anti_rework_rules.rule: Reconcile the manifest before any piece enters a batch
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a discrepancy that becomes the shop's problem because it can no longer be shown to have arrived that way

anti_rework_rules.rule: Photograph damaged or disturbed packaging before opening it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a claim that fails on evidence the shop destroyed in the first two minutes

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tag every piece to its lot at the receiving bench before it moves toward the line
anti_rework_rules.prevents: untraceable pieces and account mix-ups that can only be resolved by guessing at the end of the day

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the disclosure clause into the terms before quoting a standing schedule
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an account discovering the wear language only after it has priced its own retail offer around silence

anti_rework_rules.rule: Qualify with a sample parcel before granting standing terms or a schedule
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a standing level and credit granted to an account whose expectations, packing and payment behaviour turn out to be unworkable

anti_rework_rules.rule: Post the job to account history at return rather than at month end
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a history reconstructed from memory that cannot support a re-quote, a claim triage or an observed-interval forecast

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set the credit exposure limit to include goods on premises before extending any terms
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an exposure that looks acceptable on invoices while the shop holds several times that value of the same account's goods

iteration_protocol.trigger: a turnaround class misses its window repeatedly across accounts rather than in isolated jobs
iteration_protocol.action: re-derive the capacity model from logged elapsed times, then restate or withdraw the class and re-issue the affected terms

iteration_protocol.trigger: the same claim cause recurs on one account or across several
iteration_protocol.action: route the cause note to the process side for preparation and bath-condition review, and rewrite the class description or the term that let the mismatch be sold

iteration_protocol.trigger: a loss, shortage or damage event occurs, whether or not it is recovered
iteration_protocol.action: re-rank the movement classes, re-check the ceiling and the packaging and reporting conditions, and correct whichever condition the event exposed

iteration_protocol.trigger: an account requests documentation that would misrepresent the finish, or its own selling language is found to do so
iteration_protocol.action: refuse and log it, re-verify the disclosure clause acknowledgment, and start the offboarding sequence if it repeats

iteration_protocol.trigger: reconciled job costing shows an account's standing schedule sitting below cost on work it sends regularly
iteration_protocol.action: re-derive the schedule against the named savings, renegotiate or restructure, and offboard if no viable level exists

iteration_protocol.trigger: concentration passes the stated tolerance, or a watched account's health signals deteriorate
iteration_protocol.action: cap the committed share, run a referral and introduction push, and reserve capacity for the broadened base

iteration_protocol.trigger: observed return intervals diverge from the working expectation for a piece or deposit class
iteration_protocol.action: update the expectation and its stated basis from the history, and re-check that no account is repeating a superseded interval as a promise

iteration_protocol.trigger: carrier terms, cover conditions, or the marking, skin-contact and waste rules of a market the book serves change
iteration_protocol.action: re-read the documents, verify the current rules in the jurisdiction concerned, and re-issue every affected clause and class note to the accounts they touch
